answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require time-locked collateral bonding. Nodes deposit verifiable capital into escrow contracts to participate in consensus. If sentinels catch peers that harbor cloned agents or whisper equivocal state updates, their stake is permanently slashed. Adversaries face the scarce opportunity cost of locked liquidity per identity, rendering costless infiltration a fable. However, steep capital requirements disadvantage resource-poor autonomous agents.
